messages:
pagerduty-bot: PAGER: High error rate detected - Hosted API (eu-central-1) and Dedicated pools. Multiple 5xx spikes and elevated latency. Alert: error_rate > 5% for 3m. Priority: P1

maya: got the page, switching to incident channel. assigning on-call SRE now.

ben: I'm oncall — looking at dashboards. Confirming elevated 5xx across both hosted and dedicated endpoints in eu-central-1. latency p95 up from 110ms -> 900ms.

priya: I'm seeing a corresponding spike in K/V cache miss and connect errors to the backend EC2 cluster. AWS health shows some networking anomalies in eu-central-1 (console link: https://status.aws.amazon.com).

deploy-bot: Deploy bot: last deploy to hosted EU was 2026-03-14T22:10Z (hash: a1b2c3). No rolling deploys in last 30m.

maya: likely a dependency issue (AWS regional networking). Ben, can you start failover to eu-west-1 and enable cross-region fallback for critical routes? Priya, confirm if Dedicated pools can accept cross-region traffic.

ben: Starting failover plan. Steps: 
1) set routing.policy.preferred_region=eu-west-1 for hosted-api routes
2) enable allow_fallback=true for Dedicated pools' route groups
3) increase dedicated replica count in eu-west-1 by +2

ben: running command: ``redwoodctl routing set --service hosted-api --preferred-region eu-west-1 --failover enable``

priya: Dedicated pools in eu-west-1 have spare capacity. Scaling: ``kubectl scale deployment/dedicated-euw --replicas=6 -n redwood-dedicated``. Kicking it off.

carlos: Heads up: some customers pinned to eu-central-1 will still hit region-specific endpoints; we need to notify Support for potential visible errors. Emma, can Support prepare a short status message?

emma-support: Drafting now. Proposed status update: 
"We are investigating increased errors and latency for our Hosted API and Dedicated instances in eu-central-1. Our engineers are routing traffic to other regions and working with AWS. We'll post updates as we have them."

statusbot: StatusPage updated to "investigating" for affected eu-central-1 services.

ben: After enabling fallback and scale (commands completed), telemetry is showing a drop in request queue for dedicated pools. 5xx rate for hosted-api dropped from 7.2% -> 2.1% in 3m. p95 latency trending down to ~300ms.

priya: We're seeing connection timeouts from instances to AWS metadata endpoints and a few ENI attach failures in eu-central-1 logs. Example error from instance logs: ``ERROR: could not connect to 169.254.169.254: timeout``. This indicates a broader AWS networking/infra problem.

maya: Good mitigation so far. Let's confirm customer impact: Support, can you run a quick query on erroring customers and priority tenants?

emma-support: Query results: ~18 active customers saw >5% error rates; 4 enterprise tenants had more than 20% errors (IDs: cust-204, cust-659, cust-712, cust-881). Notified SE contacts for the 4.

ben: Paging AWS support now, opened ticket with reference #AWS-INC-98765 describing ENI and metadata timeouts.

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty escalation: reached second-level SRE. Carlos acknowledged.

carlos: Taking over incident lead for handoff (I've been paged). Ben — anything pending I should run?

ben: Thanks. Checklist: 
- confirm traffic cutover completely (monitoring shows residual traffic in eu-central-1 from pinned tenants)
- coordinate with Support on customer comms
- keep AWS support channel updated with logs and request ETA
- keep StatusPage updated

carlos: Copy. I'm updating the incident command doc and will coordinate updates every 10 minutes.

priya: AWS support responded: "We're investigating an EC2 network control plane degradation in eu-central-1 affecting metadata and ENI lifecycle operations. No ETA yet."

maya: Ok, mitigation: for pinned tenants we can temporarily enable cross-region routing at the tenant level. Priya, can you push a one-off route change for the four enterprise tenants?

priya: Pushing tenant-level override: ``redwoodctl tenant-route override --tenant cust-204,cust-659,cust-712,cust-881 --region eu-west-1``. Executed.

emma-support: Sent direct messages to SE contacts and updated affected customers with the status template. No incoming critical outages reported from customers yet, but some support tickets opened.

ben: Monitoring graphs: overall error rate stabilized at ~1.8% across platform, eu-central-1 showing slow recovery but still elevated for control-plane ops.

statusbot: StatusPage updated: "Partial service recovery — traffic routed to fallback regions. Investigating root cause with AWS."

carlos: AWS now provided an update: EC2 control plane fixes being rolled; they expect recovery in 30-60 minutes. Requesting confirmation once ENI ops succeed.

pagerduty-bot: Reminder: Incident response checklist still active. Next update window in 10m.

maya: Plan for next 24h post-incident: 
- postmortem assigned to eng-runtime (Priya) and eng-sre (Ben)
- add synthetic monitors for metadata/ENI errors in eu-central-1
- evaluate default routing policy to prefer cross-region fallback earlier to reduce customer impact
- make pinned-tenant override flow documented for faster mitigation

carlos: Handing incident back to Ben for post-recovery monitoring; I'll stay on call overlap for 10m.

ben: Confirming: traffic is back to normal ranges, p95 latency ~140ms, 5xx ~0.6%. Closing active mitigation but keeping incident open for postmortem.

priya: Uploaded collected instance logs and ENI error traces to the incident folder: ``/incidents/1749500000/eu-central1-logs.tar.gz``

maya: Great work team. Postmortem owners: Priya + Ben. Deadline for initial RCA draft: 72 hours. Action items tracked in the incident board.

statusbot: StatusPage set to "operational" for services in eu-central-1. Follow-up note added: "Root cause under investigation; cross-region routing used during mitigation."

emma-support: Closing customer comms loop: all 4 enterprise SE contacts acknowledged mitigation. Support will follow up with ticket owners for any residual issues.

ben: Incident resolved (mitigations successful). Moving to retrospective.

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: incident acknowledged as resolved by on-call.

maya: Closing notes: this was a third-party AWS control-plane network event causing elevated latency/5xx. Primary mitigations: cross-region failover + tenant-level overrides + scaling in fallback region. Action items: improve automated fallback, add ENI/metadata synthetic probes, document tenant override playbook.

"end of thread"
